Estimate gene expression entropy on a Seurat object

run_entropy.Rd

This function computes gene-level entropy across neighboring cells for a specified assay in a Seurat object. It optionally saves the entropy matrix to file and/or adds it as a new assay whose name is the assay name followed by `"_entropy"`.

Usage

run_entropy(
  seu,
  assay,
  neighbors = NULL,
  neighbors_method = c("auto", "custom", "seurat"),
  neighbor_assay = assay,
  features = NULL,
  restrict_by = NULL,
  output_path = NULL,
  add_assay = TRUE,
  meta_name = NULL,
  k = 15,
  reduction = NULL,
  dims = 20,
  nfeatures = 0,
  mode = c("counts", "binary"),
  chunk_method = c("none", "auto"),
  chunk_cells = 2000,
  parallelize = FALSE,
  n_cores = parallel::detectCores() - 1L
)

Arguments

seu

A Seurat object.

assay

Character. Name of the assay used for entropy calculation.

neighbors

Optional neighbor definition. If `neighbors_method = "custom"`, this should be a named list where `neighbors[[cell_name]]` returns a vector of neighbor cell names or indices. If `neighbors_method = "seurat"`, this should be a Seurat neighbor object. If `NULL` and `neighbors_method = "auto"`, neighbors are computed internally.

neighbors_method

Character. How to obtain neighbors. One of `"auto"`, `"custom"`, or `"seurat"`. `"auto"` computes neighbors inside the function. `"custom"` uses the user-provided neighbor list in `neighbors`. `"seurat"` uses the user-provided Seurat neighbor object in `neighbors`.

neighbor_assay

Character. Assay to use for automatic neighbor computation when `neighbors_method = "auto"`. Defaults to `assay`.

features

Optional character vector of feature names (e.g. genes) to restrict the entropy computation to. If `NULL` (default), entropy is computed for all features in `assay`. Subsetting applies only to `assay` (the scored features), not to `neighbor_assay` (which defines neighborhoods). In `"counts"` mode this also reduces runtime proportionally.

restrict_by

Optional character string naming a column in `seu@meta.data` (e.g. `"celltype"`). If provided, entropy is computed within groups rather than across them. For `neighbors_method = "auto"`, neighbors are recomputed within each group so every cell gets exactly `k` neighbors from its own group. Groups with fewer than `k + 1` cells are too small to provide `k` neighbors; their cells are treated as orphans and return entropy 0, with a warning. For `"custom"` or `"seurat"`, the provided neighbor graph is pruned to within-group neighbors instead. Cells with `NA` in the column, or with no within-group neighbors, return entropy 0. If `NULL` (default), neighbors are used as-is. Works in both normal and chunked mode.

output_path

Optional character string. If provided, saves the full entropy matrix to this file using `saveRDS()`.

add_assay

Logical. If `TRUE` (default), adds the entropy matrix to the Seurat object as a new assay whose name ends in `"_entropy"`.

meta_name

Optional character string. If provided, the per-cell mean entropy is added to the Seurat object's metadata under this column name. Works independently of `add_assay`. If either `add_assay = TRUE` or `meta_name` is set, the function returns the Seurat object; if both are off, it returns a data frame of mean entropy per cell.

k

Integer. Number of nearest neighbors to use when computing neighbors internally. Must be at least 11, because the counts entropy estimator is undefined below 11 neighbors. Default is 15.

reduction

Character. Name of an existing dimensional reduction in `seu` to use for neighbor and chunk computation (e.g. `"lsi"` for ATAC). If `NULL` (default), a PCA named `"pca_<neighbor_assay>"` is computed on `neighbor_assay` and used.

dims

Integer vector or single integer. Dimensions of `reduction` to use. A single value `n` is treated as `1:n` (so `dims = 20` means `1:20`). A vector is used as given, so `dims = 2:20` skips the first component (useful for LSI/ATAC, where component 1 mostly tracks sequencing depth). Default is 20.

nfeatures

Integer. Number of variable features to select before PCA-based neighbor computation. Default is 0.

mode

Character. Entropy mode. `"counts"` uses the count-based entropy estimator (BUB precomputed table). `"binary"` binarizes the assay counts (values > 0) and computes Shannon entropy for a Bernoulli distribution across neighbors.

chunk_method

Character. Whether to use chunked computation. One of `"none"` or `"auto"`. `"none"` uses the standard approach (default). `"auto"` splits cells into biologically similar groups and processes each group independently, significantly reducing memory and runtime for large datasets. Recommended for datasets with more than 10,000 cells.

chunk_cells

Integer. Maximum number of cells per chunk when `chunk_method = "auto"`. Defaults to 2000. Values between 1000 and 5000 are recommended.

parallelize

Logical. Whether to parallelize chunk processing across multiple cores. Only applies when chunk_method = "auto". Defaults to FALSE. Not supported on Windows.

n_cores

Integer. Number of cores to use when parallelize = TRUE. Defaults to parallel::detectCores() - 1.

Value

If `add_assay = TRUE`, returns the modified Seurat object with a new assay whose name ends in `"_entropy"`. If `add_assay = FALSE`, returns a data frame of mean entropy values per cell.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("pbmc_small", package = "SeuratObject")
run_entropy(pbmc_small, assay = "RNA", k = 15, mode = "counts")
} # }
